summary: The bill immediately cancels all EPA registrations for the pesticide diquat, bans sale and use of existing stocks, and revokes any food tolerances allowing its residues.

scores.thoughts: The bill cancels registration of a pesticide and revokes related tolerances but contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. It has no bearing on government spending levels.
The bill makes no changes to tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection mechanisms.
While the bill addresses pesticide residues in food, it does not alter healthcare delivery, insurance, coverage models, or public vs. private healthcare systems.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
The bill contains nothing concerning immigration pathways, border enforcement, or immigrant protections.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military or defense spending or policy.

The bill explicitly deems diquat to cause unreasonable adverse effects on the environment under FIFRA, mandates cancellation of all registrations, prohibits sale/use of existing stocks, and requires revocation of food tolerances. This constitutes a direct expansion of environmental protections through stricter pesticide regulation.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill concerns an agricultural pesticide, not controlled substances or drug enforcement policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill has no fiscal provisions that would affect deficits or debt reduction strategies.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions relate to foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil rights enforcement.
